$comment: D-PP-IF-UNSIGNED-INTMAX (C 6.10.1p4): a `#if`/`#elif` controlling expression is evaluated with every integer type acting as intmax_t/uintmax_t. BOTH HALVES were broken and the anchor knew about neither correctly. (a) WIDTH: `pp_if_eval.cpp`'s `parsePrimary` stamped every literal leaf `TypeKind::I32`, so `intOpDomain` ran the WHOLE evaluator in 32-BIT SIGNED -- not the 'signed int64' the anchor and the source comment both claimed -- and `wrapToIntTarget` truncated both operands before every comparison, so `#if 9223372036854775807 > 0` ('is INT64_MAX positive') took the FALSE arm, as did `#if 3000000000 > 0` and `#if 2147483647 + 1 > 0`: ordinary signed code with no unsigned suffix anywhere. (b) SIGNEDNESS: the literal's unsignedness was discarded at that same leaf, so `#if -1 < 0u` ran a SIGNED comparison and answered the opposite of both references. ★ THE ANCHOR CALLED THIS 'NOT silently wrong -- fail-loud' and 'Priority: normal (rare)' for four months. It is neither: DSS compiled the OPPOSITE branch from a unanimous gcc + clang with no diagnostic and exit 0 -- a different program, silently. 13 of 23 measured cells took the wrong arm. ★★ WHY THE MISLABEL SURVIVED, WHICH IS THE REASON THIS EXAMPLE IS SHAPED THE WAY IT IS: every instrument pointed at the anchor asserted that the code COMPILED, and a wrong-branch selection is a perfectly successful compile of the wrong program. So every cell here is EXIT-CODE DISCRIMINATING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS -- each `#if` writes a different value per arm and `main` returns 42 only if all 22 cells chose the arm gcc and clang choose; the scaling `ok*2-2` keeps a single wrong branch off 42 by arithmetic accident. The anchor's own cited witness, `#if 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFu == -1`, was the ONE shape that came out right, and by coincidence (both sides landed on int64 -1) -- the cell least able to show the defect was the one it chose, so it is pinned here too. ★ THE FIX IS CONFIG-DRIVEN AND ADDS NO SECOND OWNER: `preprocessorLiteralSignedness` (core/types/integer_literal_ladder.hpp) runs the LANGUAGE'S OWN `semantics.integerLiteralTyping` candidate ladder -- same suffix match, same radix classification, same order -- at PHASE-4 WIDTHS, and `intOpDomain`/`applyBinaryInt` already implement C's usual arithmetic conversions over the resulting (I64,U64) pair, so no new arithmetic and no parallel truth table were written. ⚠ IT IS NOT `typeIntegerLiteral` WITH THE WIDTH IGNORED, and that distinction is measured: the ordinary 6.4.4.1 ladder types `0xFFFFFFFF` as `unsigned int`, and carrying that signedness into phase 4 makes `#if 0xFFFFFFFF > -1` take the FALSE arm while BOTH references take the TRUE one -- in phase 4 the only integer types are intmax_t and uintmax_t, so signedness is re-decided at 64 bits. The adjacent pair `0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF > -1` (signed) and `0x8000000000000000 > -1` (unsigned) pins that boundary at INTMAX_MAX exactly, and the `u`-suffix cells are the control against a magnitude-only reading. ⓘ CONSEQUENCE: the rule takes NO DataModel -- at phase-4 widths every candidate is 64 bits, so a WIDTH model cannot reach the answer, and `#if -1 < 0x80000000L` is the same branch on LP64 and LLP64 (which is what both references do). Reference control, each probed SEPARATELY with the taken arm read from the EMITTED OBJECT via `nm`, never from an exit code: gcc 13.3.0 -std=c2x and clang 18.1.3 -std=c23 agree on all 22 cells, including the CONTROL `#if 2 + 2 == 4`, so this example demonstrates AGREEMENT and is not merely a collection of divergences. RED-ON-DISABLE, ✔MEASURED 2026-08-27 with four ISOLATED arms, each asserting build rc=0 + object md5 MOVED and RETURNED + reds read by NAME through ctest: (M1) keep the ladder's signedness but evaluate at 32 bits -> 3 named pins red and this example **exits 26**; (M2) keep width 64 but force every literal signed -> 5 named pins red and this example **exits 24**. Two halves, two different wrong exit codes, so the arms cannot be confused for each other. ⚠ (M3) reverting `evaluate()`'s closing `asInt64` -> `asBool` is **GREEN** and this example still exits 42 -- the plan predicted that arm would go red and it did NOT, because `intmaxOperand` stores the raw bit pattern in the INT64 arm (required: `applyUnaryInt` bridges through `asInt64`) where that verb always succeeds. The change stays as contract correctness, not as a behaviour fix, and is labelled that way at the site. (CONTROL) inserting one comment LINE moves the md5 and stays green -- which is why a moved md5 is never on its own evidence that a pin points at the change.
